stories.title: Extract the type scale into tokens.css (closes W-3) -- pure refactor
stories.completionNotes:
DONE (commit f48b3c6). 82 bare `font-size: Npx` in dashboard.css -> 5 scale tokens declared in tokens.css and mirrored into dashboard.css :root (the mirror is the established pattern -- dashboard.html links ONLY dashboard.css, so an SSOT-only drop would leave the panel unsized with a green suite; BL-027 lesson). Values are the PRE-F-127 shipped scale: hero 40 / primary 20 / secondary 14 / label 12 / meta 10. US-540-a sets 44/34/26/20/15 by editing the SSOT + the mirror -- nothing below :root changes again.

*** ONE DEVIATION, RATIFY BEFORE CLOSING THE SPRINT -- filed as offices/pm/issues/I-us539-type-scale-collapse-is-not-pixel-identical.md. AC3 asks for BOTH five tokens AND 'renders visually identical'. The file shipped 15 DISTINCT sizes (8/9/10/11/12/13/14/15/17/18/20/22/30/34/40); 15 values do not fit in 5 slots, so the two clauses are mutually exclusive on this file. I took the COLLAPSE, because the pixel-identical alternative (5 tokens + ~10 extra tokens holding the off-scale sizes) BREAKS US-540-a: that story is specified as setting FIVE values, and would leave ten stale -- the 'edits that drift' problem, just smaller. Every off-scale rule rounds UP to its tier, so NOTHING on the panel got smaller. Moves: 34/30/22->hero(3 rules), 18/17/15->primary(6), 13->secondary(21), 11->label(14), 9/8->meta(3); the other 35 rules already sat on a scale value. The one call worth Iris's eye: the STOP takeover directive goes 22->40 -- forced, because Spool 6d requires it outrank its base rule (.takeover-directive, which landed on primary), and a collapse onto one tier would have turned a SAFETY guard red. 'PULL OVER NOW' at 40px mono is ~340px of the 442px available; fits on paper, EYEBALL IT ON THE PI when US-540-a re-verifies (which raises hero to 44). ***

TWO PRE-EXISTING SAFETY GUARDS read font sizes with a raw-px regex (test_dashboard_stop_tier_safety::test_stopTakeover_directiveIsLargerThanBaseCopy, test_dtc_detail_hierarchy::test_directiveBand_isLargerThanTheDetailBodyBaseCopy). Tokenizing would have left them reading 'size absent' -- one dies on a None match, the other silently compares -1. A refactor that blinds a safety guard is worse than the drift it fixed. Both now resolve var(--fs-*) through the scale via ONE shared helper, tests/ui/css_type_scale.py, which also carries the LINE-ANCHORED ruleBlock(): a plain substring search for '.takeover-directive {' finds the STOP OVERRIDE first (declared earlier in the sheet), so a naive guard compares the override against ITSELF and reports a hierarchy that does not exist. My first cut had exactly that bug and the new test caught it (40 <= 40) -- the pre-existing suite had already solved it, which is why only my new test went red.

NEW GATE tests/ui/test_dashboard_type_scale.py (17 tests). Every assertion is an ABSENCE check, so it ships with a NEGATIVE CONTROL: the bare-px detector is driven against a stylesheet that DOES carry drift and must report it, and against a `--fs-hero: 40px` declaration it must NOT. Without the pair, a typo in the pattern reads as a green gate over a file full of literals. Also gated: font-size right-hand sides are ONLY a scale token or the deliberate `inherit` on .detail-value (US-491 load-bearing -- binding a token there re-breaks the tier ramp and looks tidier doing it); no SIXTH --fs-* token (sprawl comes back one token at a time); scale strictly descending (survives US-540-a by asserting ORDER not numbers).

GATE RUN SYNCHRONOUSLY: tests/ui/ ALL 720 passed. ruff clean on 4 touched .py. PM: this touches a SHARED stylesheet + 2 existing test files, so tests/ui/ is worth the integration re-run; no src/ or Python runtime code touched, so the wider suite is low-risk. GOTCHA FOR THE NEXT AGENT: a comment containing the literal string '@import' fails test_dashboard_brand_font_payload + test_dashboard_fidelity_pass -- both scan the raw text for it (offline-kiosk guard, correctly). I reworded the comment; do NOT weaken the guard.
acceptance: add a type scale to specs/UI/tokens.css: --fs-hero / --fs-primary / --fs-secondary / --fs-label / --fs-meta (values SET in US-540; this story just establishes the tokens + wiring)
replace the ~83 hardcoded `font-size: Npx` in dashboard.css with token refs; DoD: NO bare `font-size: Npx` left in dashboard.css (a grep gate)
PURE REFACTOR -- no visual change vs the current shipped sizes (map each existing px to the nearest token, values unchanged here); ships + verifies independently of US-540
ruff/lint clean; a probe/test confirms zero bare px font-sizes remain

validationCriteria.action: grep dashboard.css for `font-size:` with a px literal after the refactor
validationCriteria.outcome: zero hardcoded px font-sizes; all reference the tokens.css scale; dashboard renders visually identical to before

conditionalOutcomes: US-539 is the HARD prerequisite for US-540 (Iris: without tokenizing first, US-540 becomes 83 edits that drift). No design gate -- pure refactor.
stories.goal: As a maintainer, I want font sizes to come from a small set of tokens so the legibility fix is one scale change, not 83 scattered edits that drift back.

stories.title: Set the type-scale token VALUES for 3.5in legibility (44/34/26/20/15)
stories.completionNotes:
DONE code-side. The scale is set to Iris's 44/34/26/20/15 in the SSOT (specs/UI/tokens.css) and the hand-mirror in dashboard.css :root -- TEN LINES OF VALUES AND TWO COMMENT BLOCKS, nothing below :root touched. That is US-539 paying off exactly as scoped: the pre-F-127 panel would have needed 82 edits for this.

*** THE VALUES ARE NOT FINAL AND THE STORY SAYS SO -- DO NOT LET THE GREEN SUITE READ AS ACCEPTANCE. Two things are still owed, NEITHER closable on the dev box: (1) acceptance is IN-CAR, seated, at arm's length; (2) AC2 (Atlas display-pipeline) requires the output mode be confirmed PANEL-NATIVE **BEFORE** the values are called final -- if the Pi is rendering 1080p into a 480x320 panel, every glyph is scale-up-then-downsampled soft and the floor is HIGHER than 34. That confirmation is US-552, still open in this sprint. ORDER MATTERS: land US-552, THEN read the panel, THEN ratify or move these five numbers. A dev-box browser cannot see the defect this AC exists to catch. ***

WHAT TO EYEBALL FIRST, in order: (a) the STOP takeover directive 'PULL OVER NOW' -- 40px mono was already ~340px of the 442px available after US-539's forced 22->40 move, and hero is now 44, so this is the line most likely to wrap or clip, and it is a SAFETY surface; (b) any card carrying 4 facts -- secondary 14->26 is the biggest proportional jump in the scale (+86%) and card capacity is what US-540-b re-lays to ~3 facts/card, so overflow seen NOW is US-540-b's problem, not a reason to shrink the scale back; (c) the version chip / IMU tape furniture at meta 15 (was 10) -- the one tier where growth costs layout and buys little, since it is parked-read micro-copy.

NEW GATE tests/ui/test_dashboard_type_scale_values.py (8 tests). The five values are PINNED, not bounded, and the header says why: a pure '>= 34' floor test would have passed BEFORE this story ran (the old hero was 40) and would still pass if a later edit pushed hero to 90 and overflowed every card. Pinned means the next deliberate change edits one line and declares itself. Alongside the pin, the INTENT is asserted separately so it survives a value edit: driver-must-read tiers (hero/primary) >= the [EXACT:34] floor; label/meta strictly under the 26px non-critical ceiling; no tier smaller than its pre-F-127 value (F-127 travelling backwards is a real failure mode -- an overflow fix under deadline is exactly how a tier gets quietly shrunk). Two tests resolve the tokens THROUGH a real rule (.tile-value, and the STOP directive) rather than only reading :root, because a value that never reaches the surface is the failure the mirror exists to prevent -- reading :root alone would have gone green on the SSOT-only drop that US-539's notes warn about.

GATE RUN SYNCHRONOUSLY IN-LOOP: full tests/ui/ = 695 passed, exit 0 (283s); the focused 5-file gate (new values + US-539 scale + both safety guards + token SSOT) = 85 passed. ruff clean on the new test. NOTE FOR PM: my Sprint-73 note said 'tests/ui = 720'; the honest count on this tree is 695 BEFORE my +8. I have not chased the discrepancy (older number, different collection, not re-derived) -- treat 695+8=703 as the current baseline and disregard the 720. No src/ or Python runtime code touched; nothing outside the two stylesheets + one new test file changed, so wider-suite risk is low.
acceptance: set the type-scale token values (Iris): hero 44 / primary 34 / secondary 26 / label 20 / meta 15 (px on the 480x320 stage). [FLOOR RULE] driver-must-read >= [EXACT:34]px; anything <26px non-critical only. Depends US-539 (tokens exist). Acceptance IN-CAR (arm's length, seated). CAVEAT: unverified panel downsampling may raise the floor -- re-verify on hardware, do NOT call values final. ruff clean

[Atlas display-pipeline finding] the deploy pins NO HDMI/KMS output mode -> the Pi likely outputs 1080p into a 480x320-native panel -> lossy scale-up-then-downsample softens every glyph (raises the floor). Acceptance: confirm output mode == panel native (or pin it -- see US-552) BEFORE calling the 44/34/26/20/15 values final. Re-verify the values AFTER the mode is confirmed

stories.title: Pin Pi HDMI/KMS output to the panel-native 480x320 (kill downsampling)
acceptance: [Atlas A-16 display-pipeline fidelity] on the Pi (when on) read the actual output mode (kmsprint / xrandr). If it is NOT the panel's native 480x320, PIN the output to native in the deploy (KMS/HDMI mode). Eliminates the scale-up-then-downsample resampling AND renders the US-540 type scale 1:1 -- a distinct legibility lever alongside the font work
DoD: deploy sets the output mode; post-deploy the Pi reports the native mode; the type scale renders without resample-softening. ruff clean
